title: The back-of-mouth hum: /ŋ/
goal: Practise /ŋ/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Raise the back of the tongue to the soft roof of the mouth and let air pass through the nose. In sing, do not add a separate g sound after the nasal.
spelling: ng in sing represents /ŋ/. Words such as finger can include an additional /g/.
task: Ask who owns a ring. Keep ring to one syllable.
story: May can sing. Ben joins the song.
reviewPrompt: Return to day 15, 22, 26, 28. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

articulation.label: sing
articulation.alt: sing: /s/ → /ɪ/ → /ŋ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/ŋ/: Back of tongue at soft palate; air through nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
